title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs
content:
Context / summary:
- Sporadic higher 5xx and timeouts for requests routed to eu-west-1 between ~2026-03-03T08:15Z and 2026-03-03T10:40Z.
- Platform smart-routing triggered fallback policy to use model-variant 'gptx-q4f' (cheaper/quantized) when preferred variant exhausted.
- Symptoms: increased tail latency (p95->p99 spike), some token stream aborts, user-visible 503s.
- This doc is my scratchpad of commands, logs, hypotheses and next steps.

Timeline (local notes):
- 08:05Z: Ops alert for elevated error rate in EU region (internal alert id: eu-routing-err-20260303).
- 08:10Z: first obvious spike in Gateway 5xxs, coincident with a small autoscale effort in dedicated cluster eu-west-1.
- 08:22Z: Canary fallback kicked in (policy: prefer-dedicated-region -> fallback to hosted-variant -> then regional failover). Logs show fallback decisions.
- 09:00Z: partial recovery after increasing reserved slots in dedicated pool, but intermittent errors until 10:40Z.

Commands I ran (terminal breadcrumbs):
- Check routing decisions from routing service API:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTING_KEY" https://routing-api.internal.redwood/v1/decisions?request_id=abc123 | jq '.decision'
  -> returned: "fallback_to_variant=gptx-q4f, reason=capacity_exhausted, region=eu-west-1"

- Check health of dedicated pool pods (k8s):
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=dedicated-pool-eu -o wide
  # Several pods in CrashLoopBackOff around 08:06-08:15 (restarts: 4-6)

- Grep logs for fallback entries on router nodes:
  kubectl -n redwood logs svc/router-0 | rg "fallback_to_variant|capacity_exhausted" -n -i --line-number | tail -n 40
  # sample: 2026-03-03T08:22:13Z router-0 INFO fallback_to_variant=gptx-q4f reason=pool_capacity_exhausted pool=dedicated-eu shard=3

- Check autoscaler decisions and cloud metrics (internal CLI):
  rwctl autoscaler status --pool dedicated-eu --since 2026-03-03T07:50Z
  -> saw repeated scale-up requests throttled by quota; some nodes marked Unavailable by cloud provider for ~10m.

- Replayed a failing request locally to reproduce latency behavior:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY" -d '{"model":"gptx","input":"hello"}' https://proxy.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/generate -v
  -> 504 timeout after 30s when routed to fallback variant; direct to hosted-gptx endpoint succeeded but with higher latency (~1.2s vs baseline 200ms).

Observed error snippets (copied raw):
- Router log:
  2026-03-03T08:22:13Z router-0 INFO request_id=abc123 decision=fallback_to_variant=gptx-q4f reason=pool_capacity_exhausted
- Worker log:
  2026-03-03T08:08:47Z worker-5 WARN kv-cache-miss, cold-start-sequence, prep-latency=312ms
- Serving runtime error (when failover produced 5xx):
  ERROR handle_request: upstream_write: broken pipe
  stack: serve::connection::write_frame -> tokio::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe

Hypotheses (rough):
- Primary: Dedicated eu-west-1 pool lost capacity unexpectedly (cloud provider maintenance or node eviction) -> autoscaler tried to replenish but hit provider quota -> routing fallback policy moved traffic to quantized variant leading to higher CPU pressure and some unhandled edge cases causing stream aborts.
- Secondary: Fallback policy priority list includes region fallbacks that are slower; we may be routing to model variants that are not fully warmed/cached (no KV cache priming) causing cold-start tail latencies.
- Tertiary: A recent rollout of routing rule change (PR #1823) adjusted fallback thresholds too aggressively (threshold: available_slots < 10 -> fallback immediately).

Things I checked and ruling out so far:
- Config mismatch: verified routing-config for customer-tier mapping (yaml) matches repo: git show origin/main:configs/routing/eu.yml | rg 'fallback_threshold' -> value was 10 (intended).
- Model-variant compatibility: variant gptx-q4f is compatible with hosted inference path (no schema mismatch).
- Network partition: no broad network outage in region according to provider status page (only sporadic node unavailability).

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Increased dedicated pool capacity by temporarily bumping min_replicas for dedicated-eu -> restart/pod pressure reduced.
- Toggled fallback_sensitivity from 10 -> 4 for 30 minutes (rollback if errors persist).
- Posted to Slack #inc-prod-routing and paged SRE for cloud quota review.

Remaining unknowns / follow-ups:
- Need to correlate provider node unavailability with time windows; ask infra to pull provider event logs for 07:30-09:30Z.
- Confirm whether recent routing PR (redwood/routing#1823) changed metrics used by autoscaler or fallback engine.
- Add more granular logging in router for fallback decision context: include pool_free_slots, estimated_warm_kv_hits, peak_inflight_tokens.
- Investigate stream abort root cause (BrokenPipe) when writing to downstream worker after fallback; could be worker OOM or SIGPIPE due to client disconnect.

Suggested next steps (actionable):
1) Reproduce locally with controlled capacity drain: run load test that simulates pool slot exhaustion and observe fallback behavior end-to-end.
2) Add a temporary guard in routing decision to prefer cross-region warm pools before switching to quantized variant in-place (to avoid cold-start tails).
3) Instrument warmup: when fallback_to_variant occurs, schedule async KV cache prefill for top N prefixes for that model variant.
4) Create RFC for fallback thresholds with data from past 30 incidents; propose safer defaults (e.g., threshold 3 for immediate fallback).
5) Open INF-4240 assigned to Priya for root cause investigation and link to this note.

Notes / todo (personal):
- Talk to Priya tomorrow 09:00 PT to walk through autoscaler logs.
- Add a smoke test in CI that checks fallback path correctness (ensure stream keepalive + proper backpressure).
- Follow up with cloud provider on node preemption reasons.

Random crumbs I might want later:
- Routing decision proto fields: {request_id, preferred_pool, pool_free_slots, fallback_variant, fallback_reason, timestamp, trace_id}
- Quick grep to find fallback incidents in logs: rg "fallback_to_variant" /var/log/routing/* | cut -d' ' -f1-3 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr

End of scratchpad.

-- Alex
